Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. This neuron's strongest (least-suppressed) responses come on ordinary mid-clause function words — the modal "would", determiner "a", pronoun "you", preposition "in" — while it is most strongly suppressed on finite present-tense verbs immediately following a named subject ("Bob offers", "Larry checks", "Lisa is") and on sentence-final periods, so it looks like a syntactic-position signal rather than a semantic detector.
